title: OSHA crane signals practice questions
description: Practice questions on OSHA crane signals: when a signal person is required, signal types, new signals, lost signals and stops (29 CFR 1926.1419).

questions.topic: When a signal person is required
questions.question: In 1926.1419(a)(1), what does "point of operation" mean?

options.A: The operator's cab and its operational controls
options.B: The load travel or the area near or at load placement
options.C: The area within the swing radius of the rotating superstructure
options.D: The spot where the outriggers are set

questions.explanation: A signal person is required when "The point of operation, meaning the load travel or the area near or at load placement, is not in full view of the operator."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: When a signal person is required
questions.question: Under 1926.1419(a)(2), what condition makes a signal person required while the equipment is traveling?

options.A: The equipment is traveling on a public road
options.B: The equipment is traveling with the boom fully extended
options.C: The equipment is traveling at night
options.D: The view in the direction of travel is obstructed

questions.explanation: 1926.1419(a)(2) applies "When the equipment is traveling, the view in the direction of travel is obstructed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: When a signal person is required
questions.question: Under 1926.1419(a)(3), who may determine that site specific safety concerns make a signal person necessary?

options.A: Either the operator or the person handling the load
options.B: Only the controlling entity
options.C: Only a qualified evaluator (third party)
options.D: Only the crane manufacturer

questions.explanation: A signal person must be provided when, "Due to site specific safety concerns, either the operator or the person handling the load determines that it is necessary."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Types of signals and hand signals
questions.question: How does 1926.1401 define the "Standard Method" that 1926.1419(c)(1) requires when hand signals are used?

options.A: The signals printed in the equipment manufacturer's operating manual
options.B: Any set of hand signals that the operator and signal person agree on before the lift
options.C: The protocol in appendix A of this subpart for hand signals
options.D: A national consensus standard for radio signals

questions.explanation: "Standard Method means the protocol in appendix A of this subpart for hand signals." Under 1926.1419(c)(1), "When using hand signals, the Standard Method must be used".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Types of signals and hand signals
questions.question: How does 1926.1401 define an "audible signal"?

options.A: A signal shown on a video monitor in the cab
options.B: A flashing light visible from the cab
options.C: A signal made by a distinct sound or series of sounds
options.D: A signal that only the crane's own horn can make

questions.explanation: "Audible signal means a signal made by a distinct sound or series of sounds." The definition adds that examples "include, but are not limited to, sounds made by a bell, horn, or whistle."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Types of signals and hand signals
questions.question: Under the exception in 1926.1419(c)(1), when may non-standard hand signals be used?

options.A: Where use of the Standard Method is infeasible, or where an operation or use of an attachment is not covered in the Standard Method
options.B: Whenever the operator and signal person prefer them
options.C: Only when radio communication has failed
options.D: Only on equipment that is traveling

questions.explanation: "Where use of the Standard Method for hand signals is infeasible, or where an operation or use of an attachment is not covered in the Standard Method, non-standard hand signals may be used in accordance with paragraph (c)(2) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Non-standard hand signals and new signals
questions.question: Before an operation that uses non-standard hand signals, who must contact each other and agree on the signals?

options.A: The operator and the competent person only
options.B: The signal person and a qualified evaluator
options.C: The employer and the crane manufacturer
options.D: The signal person, operator, and lift director (where there is one)

questions.explanation: "the signal person, operator, and lift director (where there is one) must contact each other prior to the operation and agree on the non-standard hand signals that will be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Non-standard hand signals and new signals
questions.question: Under 1926.1419(d), who must demonstrate that new signals meet the rule's conditions before they may be used?

options.A: The operator
options.B: The employer
options.C: The signal person
options.D: The crane manufacturer

questions.explanation: New signals "may be used where the employer demonstrates that" one of the conditions in 1926.1419(d)(1) or (d)(2) is met.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Non-standard hand signals and new signals
questions.question: Which of these is one of the options in 1926.1419(d) for using new signals?

options.A: The new signals are printed in the operator's manual
options.B: The new signals comply with a national consensus standard that provides at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals
options.C: The new signals are used only in daylight
options.D: The new signals are approved by the lift director

questions.explanation: 1926.1419(d)(2) allows new signals where "The new signals comply with a national consensus standard that provides at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals." Option (d)(1) is that the new signals themselves "provide at least equally effective communication".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Suitability and keeping the signal link
questions.question: Under 1926.1419(e), what must be appropriate for the site conditions?

options.A: Only the signal person's high-visibility clothing
options.B: Only the radio frequency used
options.C: Only the hand-signal chart posted in the cab
options.D: Both the signals used and the means of transmitting the signals to the operator

questions.explanation: "The signals used (hand, voice, audible, or new), and means of transmitting the signals to the operator (such as direct line of sight, video, radio, etc.), must be appropriate for the site conditions."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Suitability and keeping the signal link
questions.question: Under 1926.1431(k)(9), with whom must employees being hoisted on a personnel platform remain in direct communication?

options.A: The signal person (where used), or the operator
options.B: The competent person on the ground only
options.C: The lift director only
options.D: The employer's site safety office

questions.explanation: "Employees being hoisted must remain in direct communication with the signal person (where used), or the operator."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Suitability and keeping the signal link
questions.question: How does 1926.1401 define a "dedicated channel"?

options.A: A radio channel shared by all trades on the site
options.B: A channel assigned to the site by the crane rental company
options.C: A line of communication assigned by the employer who controls the communication system to only one signal person and crane/derrick or to a coordinated group of cranes/derricks/signal person(s)
options.D: A telephone line between the operator and the manufacturer

questions.explanation: "Dedicated channel means a line of communication assigned by the employer who controls the communication system to only one signal person and crane/derrick or to a coordinated group of cranes/derricks/signal person(s)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Suitability and keeping the signal link
questions.question: Where the employer chooses a dedicated spotter as the measure under 1926.1408(b)(4)(ii), what equipment must the spotter use where necessary?

options.A: Equipment that enables the dedicated spotter to communicate directly with the operator
options.B: A video camera mounted on the boom tip
options.C: An air horn to warn other crews on the site
options.D: A range control warning device set to stop movement

questions.explanation: The dedicated spotter must, "Where necessary, use equipment that enables the dedicated spotter to communicate directly with the operator."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Safety problems and stop signals
questions.question: Under 1926.1419(g), what must the operator do on becoming aware of a safety problem and needing to communicate with the signal person?

options.A: Finish the current lift, then radio the signal person
options.B: Report the problem to the competent person in writing
options.C: Lower the load at full speed
options.D: Safely stop operations

questions.explanation: "If the operator becomes aware of a safety problem and needs to communicate with the signal person, the operator must safely stop operations."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Safety problems and stop signals
questions.question: After the operator stops for a safety problem under 1926.1419(g), when may operations resume?

options.A: When the competent person signs a restart form
options.B: When the operator and signal person agree that the problem has been resolved
options.C: When the lift director orders a restart
options.D: When the employer's safety manager arrives

questions.explanation: "Operations must not resume until the operator and signal person agree that the problem has been resolved."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Safety problems and stop signals
questions.question: An employee is hoisted in pile driving operations with a telescopic boom crane. What does 1926.1431(p)(2) require to prevent two-blocking?

options.A: Only a clearly visible mark on the cable
options.B: Either a mark on the cable or a spotter, at the employer's choice
options.C: A clearly marked cable and a spotter in direct communication with the operator to inform the operator when the marked point is reached
options.D: A horn signal from the employee before each hoist

questions.explanation: "For telescopic boom cranes: Clearly mark the cable (so that it can be easily seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, and use a spotter who is in direct communication with the operator to inform the operator when this point is reached." The "or" choice applies to lattice boom cranes.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Who signals, direction and multiple cranes
questions.question: For equipment other than tower cranes, the operator's trainer and the operator-in-training must be in direct line of sight of each other. How does 1926.1427(b)(4)(iii) say they must also communicate?

options.A: Verbally or by hand signals
options.B: Only by radio on a dedicated channel
options.C: Only through a separate signal person
options.D: Only by written notes passed to the cab

questions.explanation: "For equipment other than tower cranes: The operator's trainer and the operator-in-training must be in direct line of sight of each other. In addition, they must communicate verbally or by hand signals."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Who signals, direction and multiple cranes
questions.question: Where a signal person is in communication with more than one crane/derrick, what does 1926.1419(m)(1) require the signal person to do for each signal, prior to giving the function/direction?

options.A: Sound an audible warning
options.B: Repeat the previous signal
options.C: Obtain the lift director's approval
options.D: Identify the crane/derrick the signal is for

questions.explanation: Under 1926.1419(m)(1), "for each signal, prior to giving the function/direction, the signal person must identify the crane/ derrick the signal is for". The other option, (m)(2), is to "use an equally effective method of identifying which crane/derrick the signal is for."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Related definitions and work area communication
questions.question: How does 1926.1401 describe a "qualified evaluator (not a third party)" for signal persons?

options.A: An OSHA compliance officer assigned to the site
options.B: A person employed by the signal person's employer who has demonstrated that he/she is competent in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Qualification Requirements in this subpart for a signal person
options.C: Any certified crane operator on the site
options.D: An employee of the crane manufacturer

questions.explanation: "Qualified evaluator (not a third party) means a person employed by the signal person's employer who has demonstrated that he/she is competent in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Qualification Requirements in this subpart for a signal person."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Related definitions and work area communication
questions.question: Under 1926.1424(a)(3)(i), before an employee goes to a location in the swing radius hazard area that is out of view of the operator, what must the employee (or someone instructed by the employee) ensure?

options.A: That the load has been landed
options.B: That a competent person escorts the employee
options.C: That the operator is informed that he/she is going to that location
options.D: That the barriers around the hazard area are taken down

questions.explanation: "Before an employee goes to a location in the hazard area that is out of view of the operator, the employee (or someone instructed by the employee) must ensure that the operator is informed that he/she is going to that location."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1424, Work area control (as of Nov 4, 2026)
